current_tip: "conseguir" (e→i) + infinitive = to manage to. Irregular yo: consigo. "Cuando" + present for habitual.
fixed_tip: 'Para' expresses purpose, destination, or recipient: 'para descansar' (in order to rest), 'para ti' (for you).

current_tip: "decir que" + subjunctive for commands/advice. "Dejara" = imperfect subjunctive (past context). "Dejar de" = to stop.
fixed_tip: 'Enojar' follows the gustar pattern: the annoying thing is the subject. 'Me enoja que...' = it angers me that...

current_tip: "gustaría que" + imperfect subjunctive. Conditional + que → subjunctive. "Vinieras" from "venir" (irregular subjunctive stem).
fixed_tip: Indefinite articles match gender: 'un' (masc.), 'una' (fem.). 'Un sitio' but 'una botella'. Plural 'unos/unas' means 'some'.

current_tip: "se necesitan" (passive se, plural agreement). "Cada uno" = each one (invariable).
fixed_tip: 'Al' is the mandatory contraction of 'a + el': 'al parque', 'al cine'. It only happens with masculine singular 'el'.

current_tip: passive participle as adjective: "incluido" agrees with "desayuno" (masc). "Estar" + past participle for states resulting from actions.
fixed_tip: 'Doler' works like 'gustar': the body part is the subject. 'Me duele la cabeza' = the head hurts to me. Plural: 'me duelen los pies'.

current_tip: "hay que" (impersonal must) + infinitive. "Antes de" + infinitive = before doing.
fixed_tip: 'Poder' stem-changes o→ue: puedo, puedes, puede. Used for ability and polite requests: '¿puede traer...?'

current_tip: passive: "fue aprobada" (ser + past participle, agreeing with "ley" = feminine). "Por unanimidad" = unanimously.

current_tip: "recetar" = to prescribe. 3rd person plural "recetaron" with no stated subject = impersonal "they prescribed me."
fixed_tip: 'Mucho' agrees when adjective (muchos amigos) but is invariable as adverb (trabaja mucho). Gender/number match only with nouns.

current_tip: double object pronouns: "se lo" = it to him/her. "Se" replaces "le" before "lo/la." "Hacer caso" = to pay attention.

current_tip: "atreverse a" + infinitive = to dare to. Reflexive verb. "No me atrevo" = I don't dare.

current_tip: "Salí corriendo" – the gerund (-ando/-iendo) after a verb of motion describes HOW the action was done. Like English "I ran out" but literally "I left running."

current_tip: "llevar" + gerund + "desde" = have been doing since. "Llevar" for duration is a key alternative to present perfect.
fixed_tip: 'Hay' = there is / there are. Unlike 'ser/estar', 'hay' is the same for singular and plural. Comes from 'haber'.
